embedded.title: Windows User Rights Assignment
embedded.description: Manage which accounts hold a Windows user right or privilege.
embedded.markdownDescription:
The `Microsoft.Windows/UserRightsAssignment` resource manages which accounts hold a Windows user right or privilege, the settings under **Local Policies > User Rights Assignment** in the Local Security Policy console.

[Online documentation][01]

[01]: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/dsc/reference/microsoft.windows/userrightsassignment/resource

right.title: User right
right.description: The user right or privilege constant, for example 'SeServiceLogonRight' (Log on as a service).
right.markdownDescription:
The constant of the user right or privilege to manage, such as `SeServiceLogonRight` (_Log on as a service_). These are the names that the LSA, `secedit` templates, Group Policy and security benchmarks use. Each instance manages one right.

[Online documentation][01]

[01]: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/dsc/reference/microsoft.windows/userrightsassignment/resource#right

identity.title: Identities
identity.description: The accounts that hold the right. Accepts 'DOMAIN\Name', a bare account name, a well-known name such as 'Everyone', a SID string such as 'S-1-5-32-544', or the secedit form '*S-1-5-32-544'. Returned as the canonical 'DOMAIN\Name', or as the SID string when the SID does not resolve to an account. An empty array means that no one holds the right. Required for set and test.
identity.markdownDescription:
The accounts that hold the right. Each entry can be an account name with its domain, a bare account name, a SID string, or a SID string prefixed with `*` as `secedit` exports it.

The resource reports each holder by its canonical name: `DOMAIN\Name`, a bare name for accounts without a domain such as `Everyone`, or the SID string when the SID doesn't resolve to an account. Specify the canonical name to make the desired state match the actual state; the resource writes an informational message for any other spelling.

An empty array means that no one holds the right. Required for **Set** and **Test**.

[Online documentation][01]

[01]: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/dsc/reference/microsoft.windows/userrightsassignment/resource#identity

items.title: Identity
items.description: An account, as 'DOMAIN\Name', a bare account name, a SID string or a SID string prefixed with '*'.

oneOf.title: Account name with domain
oneOf.description: An account name qualified with its domain or authority, such as 'BUILTIN\Administrators' or 'NT SERVICE\ALL SERVICES'. This is the canonical form for accounts that have a domain.
oneOf.markdownDescription: An account name qualified with its domain or authority, such as `BUILTIN\Administrators`, `NT SERVICE\ALL SERVICES` or `CONTOSO\svc-sql`. This is the canonical form for accounts that have a domain.

oneOf.title: Bare account name
oneOf.description: An account name without a domain, such as 'Administrators', or a well-known name that has no domain, such as 'Everyone'. Well-known names are localized, so use the name that the target system's language uses.
oneOf.markdownDescription: An account name without a domain, such as `Administrators`, or a well-known name that has no domain, such as `Everyone`. Well-known names are localized, so use the name that the target system's language uses. The resource reports an account that has a domain as `DOMAIN\Name`.

oneOf.title: SID string
oneOf.description: A security identifier, such as 'S-1-5-32-544'. A SID that doesn't resolve to an account is accepted, because Windows keeps rights assigned to deleted accounts.
oneOf.markdownDescription: A security identifier, such as `S-1-5-32-544`. A SID that doesn't resolve to an account is accepted, because Windows keeps rights assigned to deleted accounts.

oneOf.title: secedit SID
oneOf.description: A SID string prefixed with '*', the form that 'secedit' exports, such as '*S-1-5-32-544'.
oneOf.markdownDescription: A SID string prefixed with `*`, the form that `secedit` exports, such as `*S-1-5-32-544`.

setAction.title: Set action
setAction.description: How 'identity' is applied: 'replace' makes the listed accounts the only holders of the right, 'add' grants the right to the listed accounts and keeps the other holders, 'remove' revokes the right from the listed accounts only.
setAction.markdownDescription:
How the **Set** operation applies `identity` and how the **Test** operation judges it. Defaults to `replace`. DSC doesn't compare this write-only property and it never appears in the actual state.

[Online documentation][01]

[01]: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/dsc/reference/microsoft.windows/userrightsassignment/resource#setaction
markdownEnumDescriptions: The listed accounts become the only holders of the right; every other holder is revoked. An empty `identity` revokes the right from everyone.
The listed accounts are granted the right; the other holders are kept.
The listed accounts lose their direct assignment of the right; the other holders are kept. Members of a listed group can still hold the right through another group.
